formulas.title: Michaelis-Menten Equation
formulas.worked: If Vmax = 100 µmol/min, Km = 5 mM, and [S] = 5 mM: V = (100×5)/(5+5) = 50 µmol/min (half of Vmax, as expected when [S]=Km)
formulas.note: Km is the substrate concentration at which reaction velocity is half of Vmax; a low Km indicates high enzyme-substrate affinity.

formulas.title: Lineweaver-Burk Equation
formulas.worked: Plotting 1/V against 1/[S] gives a straight line whose y-intercept is 1/Vmax and whose slope is Km/Vmax
formulas.note: This double-reciprocal linearization makes it easier to determine Km and Vmax graphically from experimental data.

formulas.title: Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation
formulas.worked: For a buffer with pKa = 6.1 and a 2:1 ratio of bicarbonate to carbonic acid: pH = 6.1 + log(2) = 6.1 + 0.3 = 6.4
formulas.note: This equation describes how the pH of a buffer solution depends on the ratio of conjugate base to weak acid.

formulas.title: Gibbs Free Energy
formulas.worked: A reaction with ΔH = -20 kJ/mol, T = 298K, and ΔS = -0.05 kJ/(mol·K): ΔG = -20 - 298(-0.05) = -20+14.9 = -5.1 kJ/mol (spontaneous)
formulas.note: A negative ΔG indicates a spontaneous (exergonic) reaction; a positive ΔG indicates a non-spontaneous (endergonic) reaction.

formulas.title: ATP Yield of Glucose Oxidation
formulas.eq: ~30-32 ATP per glucose (2 from glycolysis, 2 from Krebs cycle, ~26-28 from oxidative phosphorylation)
formulas.worked: Complete aerobic oxidation of one glucose molecule via glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain yields roughly 30-32 net ATP
formulas.note: Older textbooks cite ~36-38 ATP; modern estimates are lower because of updated proton-to-ATP ratios in ATP synthase.

formulas.title: Percentage Composition Formula
formulas.eq: % element = (mass of element in compound / total molar mass) × 100
formulas.note: Used to determine what fraction of a compound's mass is contributed by a given element.

formulas.title: Dilution Formula
formulas.worked: To dilute 10 mL of a 2M stock solution to 0.5M: C1V1=C2V2 → (2)(10)=(0.5)(V2) → V2=40 mL total volume
formulas.note: Used whenever preparing a diluted solution of known concentration from a more concentrated stock.

formulas.title: Beer-Lambert Law
formulas.note: Relates the absorbance (A) of a solution to its concentration (c), the molar absorptivity (ε), and the path length (l); used in spectrophotometry to quantify biomolecules.

formulas.title: Net Reaction of Cellular Respiration
formulas.worked: One mole of glucose combines with six moles of oxygen to yield six moles each of carbon dioxide and water, releasing usable chemical energy
formulas.note: This overall equation summarizes glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation combined.

formulas.title: Net Reaction of Photosynthesis
formulas.worked: Photosynthesis is essentially the reverse of cellular respiration, storing light energy as chemical energy in glucose
formulas.note: The light reactions produce ATP, NADPH, and O2; the Calvin cycle uses ATP and NADPH to fix CO2 into glucose.

formulas.title: pH Scale Relationship
formulas.note: Each one-unit drop in pH represents a tenfold increase in hydrogen ion concentration.

typein.q: What percentage of human body mass is hydrogen, according to the lecture's table?
typein.e: Hydrogen is listed at 9.5% of body mass — the third-most abundant element listed.

typein.q: What percentage of people in developing countries, per the lecture, believe in the supernatural origin of life and diseases?
typein.e: The lecture states at least 10% of people in developed countries and 30% in developing countries believe in the supernatural origin of life and diseases, which is described as a major obstacle in disease control.
typein.t: Views on the Origin of Life

typein.q: An orbital is defined as a volume of space around the nucleus within which there is what probability of finding an electron?
typein.e: An orbital is a volume of space around the nucleus within which there is a 95% probability of finding an electron.
